account: Cosmo Artificial Intelligence of Dublin, Ireland, makes GI Genius, a program that marks suspected polyps with a box on the screen during colonoscopy. In the AID trial at three hospitals in Milan, Rome and Como, 700 patients were randomly assigned between September and November 2019 to colonoscopy with or without the program, performed by six endoscopists. FDA asked for an analysis of the 263 patients at low risk of colorectal cancer. In that group, FDA reviewers report an adenoma detection rate of 55.1% with GI Genius against 42.0% with standard colonoscopy, and 0.81 adenomas per colonoscopy against 0.57. The program caused no added adverse events. FDA granted the De Novo request on 9 April 2021. The reviewers note that race was not recorded, that most patients were presumed to be white, and that only six endoscopists in Italy took part. They write that a reduction in cancer risk would need confirmation in further trials.
